answer: The network requires each AI agent to perform remote attestation inside a distinct hardware TEE whose cryptographic identity is sealed to a basalt‑etched chip ID; the ID is recorded on the ledger with an umber‑colored proof token. When a new agent registers, validators compare the token against the current nadir of known IDs, rejecting any duplicate sealed key. To forge a fake identity an attacker must purchase a separate TEE, embed a unique basalt chip, and lock up a collateral stake of 10 ETH per node, making each Sybil cost 10 ETH plus hardware expense.
